name: Sundial-Pyre
geological_features: Radial lava flow patterns from central megavolcano
specific_features: Shadow-casting spire of unknown material at geographic center
description: Sundial-Pyre is dominated by a single megavolcano at its geographic center, from which radial lava flows extend outward like the markings on a clock face. The flows have carved channels so deep and regular that the planet's surface resembles an enormous sundial when viewed from orbit.

The atmosphere is a choking brew of sulfur dioxide and volcanic particulates, superheated to temperatures that can soften unshielded hull plating. Visibility at ground level rarely exceeds a hundred meters, and the constant volcanic lightning illuminates the haze in strobing flashes of white and orange.

At the exact center of the megavolcano's caldera stands a spire of unknown material that resists all analysis. It casts shadows across the radial lava flows with geometric precision, and spectral analysis suggests it predates the planet's volcanic activity by billions of years, as though the world formed around it.

The spire is the primary draw for expeditions to this otherwise hostile world. Its material composition remains unknown, as no sampling tool has successfully extracted even a fragment. The uranium deposits in the surrounding terrain help justify the enormous expense of operating in such extreme conditions.
